source.title: A Mesoscopic Link-Transmission-Model Able to Track Individual Vehicles
source.extraction_boundary: text declarations only; published curves, plotted values, errors, and numerical outcomes were not inspected, digitised, or encoded

topology.value: two successive directed links, link 1 upstream of link 2; link 2 has lower capacity

continuous_reference_timestep_s.uc_use: not run or compared in this preparation slice

value: one-to-one node flow is min(upstream demand, downstream supply)
integer vehicle flows in the proposed model
FIFO association of vehicles and cumulative flows

derived_mathematically.observation_horizon: 150 s, derived from the end of declared demand support rather than an explicit paper stop rule
derived_mathematically.cfl_note: the paper declares both dt=6 s and max(V,W)*dt<=L; with L=150 m and V=30 m/s, dt=6 s violates that stated condition

implementation_assumptions: map each paper link to one UC lane because lane count is not declared
treat both links as empty before the first departure
assign every unit packet the fixed route L1 to L2
treat the boundary after L2 as a free terminal sink under current UC completion semantics
integrate the piecewise demand over [0,t], floor cumulative vehicles at tick endpoints, and schedule newly resolved unit packets at that endpoint tick
use current UC ceiling-rounded positive free-flow and backward-wave lags
use current UC deterministic same-tick event and movement-allocation ordering
stop the bounded observation at 150 s
blocked_or_ambiguous: paper-declared initial link occupancies or packet placement
paper-declared route or routing rule beyond the unique two-link topology
paper-declared departure packetisation and tick-boundary convention
paper-declared tie-breaking or same-tick event ordering
paper-declared simulation stop or clearance rule
published numerical outputs and comparison tolerances, intentionally withheld until the next slice
